title: Case 1: Name and Territory of the Union (India, that is Bharat) (Article 1 • Writ Petition)
legalTheme: Part I: The Union and its Territory • Article 1
factualMatrix: Before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32), an aggrieved petitioner challenged an impugned executive notification and enforcement order issued by the Union Ministry / Central Authority under Article 1 (Name and Territory of the Union (India, that is Bharat)) of Part I (The Union and its Territory). Relying on the core guarantee that Designates the dual indigenous and modern constitutional nomenclature of the nation as "India, that is Bharat", characterizes the polity as an indestructible "Union of States", and catalogs the three territorial constituents of the Republic. and citing In re Berubari Union (1960), the petitioner sought judicial invalidation for violating constitutional limits and procedural fairness.
framingQuestions: 1. Whether the Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable under Article 1?
2. Does the Union Ministry / Central Authority's executive notification and enforcement order conform to Article 1 (Name and Territory of the Union (India, that is Bharat))?
3. How does In re Berubari Union (1960) govern the constitutional validity and relief in this matter?
modelAnswer:
1. MAINTAINABILITY: The Writ Petition before the Supreme Court of India (Article 32) is maintainable as it raises a direct constitutional question under Article 1 (Part I).

2. SUBSTANTIVE ANALYSIS (Article 1): Designates the dual indigenous and modern constitutional nomenclature of the nation as "India, that is Bharat", characterizes the polity as an indestructible "Union of States", and catalogs the three territorial constituents of the Republic. Applying the governing principle—'Indestructible Union of destructible units: Parliament can reshape states internally without their consent.'—the impugned executive notification and enforcement order by the Union Ministry / Central Authority must strictly satisfy constitutional bounds.

3. PRECEDENT (In re Berubari Union (1960)) & RELIEF: Guided by In re Berubari Union (1960), any overreach inconsistent with Article 1 is liable to be quashed or suitably restrained.
